summary.text: A 30-year-old woman, a known case of systemic lupus erythematosus with class 4 lupus nephritis for seven years, presented to a rural hospital with two months of breathlessness, cough with expectoration, fever, generalized weakness and joint pain in all four limbs. She had a rash on the abdomen and ankle, lived in a rural place and was illiterate.

Examination showed a well oriented, cooperative, conscious patient who was vitally stable, with reduced bilateral air entry, fine crackles in the upper and middle lobes and reduced limb strength. Chest X-ray, bronchoscopy and CT thorax showed a slight right pleural effusion, secretions, nodules, cavitary lesions and atelectatic bands. She was diagnosed with anemia, pneumonia and pneumonitis and was on Shelcal, Duolin inhaler and methylprednisolone.

She was referred for physiotherapy, informed about her condition and consented to therapy. For four weeks thoracic expansion exercises, spirometry, active cycle of breathing technique and the six-minute walk test were conducted; she performed pursed lip breathing and used a flutter, and the therapist performed range of motion exercises for an upper limb. A dyspnea-relieving position, bilateral active range of motion and endurance exercises are also listed in the protocol.

After four weeks, the six-minute walk distance rose from 290 to 420 and perceived exertion fell from 7 to 3. Incentive spirometry volume increased from 600 cc to 1200 cc and total lung capacity from 1.8 to 2.4 liters. Printed manual muscle testing grades rose to 5+ at all listed joints, and the authors report she breathes efficiently with improved function, pain control and quality of life.

article_limitations: Case text MMRC grade 4 conflicts with Table 3 pre-treatment MMRC grade 3; both quarantined as review-only.
Discussion statements about cardiovascular involvement and MRC grade 5 are not supported elsewhere in the case and are kept review-only.
Table 3 six-minute walk distance has no printed unit and the rate of perceived exertion scale is not defined; no units or scales were inferred.
Table 2 is a protocol; only some listed exercises are stated as performed, the rest are recorded with unknown status.
Investigations in the presentation paragraph and the diagnosis paragraph are not stated to be the same; no CBC result is reported.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected in this annotation; the four JPEGs were inspected in the separate visual target.
Discussion and introduction sentences on general SLE, sickle cell disease and literature findings are background, not patient facts.
